drafts.title: Follow a Small Movement: Mirror Play
drafts.invitation: If the child lifts a finger, use your hand to gently move in the same way, matching the motion without pressure or expectation. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Use soft, slow motion to mirror the child’s movement. Describe the action as it happens, like 'moving up' or 'turning sideways.' Avoid asking for more or faster
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child watches your hand after the movement ends.

drafts.title: Follow a Small Movement: Quiet Rhythm
drafts.invitation: If the child taps a fingertip once, let your hand follow the same small motion, keeping it gentle and unhurried. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Describe the movement as it happens, like 'a little tap' or 'a small turn.' Avoid correcting or repeating the action.
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child pauses before making the next movement.

drafts.title: Quiet Rhythm Exchange: Adult as Echo
drafts.invitation: If the child offers a quiet vocal rhythm, use your voice to softly mirror it once, then pause. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Use a quiet, gentle tone to echo the child’s rhythm exactly as offered, without embellishment or correction.
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child repeats the rhythm with slight variation after the echo.

drafts.title: Rhythm Flow: Let the Child Lead
drafts.invitation: If the child alters their quiet rhythm, let the silence follow without reaction. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Let the pause hold space—do not fill it with sound, words, or gestures.
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child returns to the rhythm with renewed focus after a pause.

drafts.title: Open Mark-Making: Trust the Process
drafts.invitation: If the child picks up the crayon and begins to move it across the paper, let them continue without comment. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Let the child lead the motion; describe only what is visible, not what it might mean.
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child pauses to look at the marks they’ve made.

drafts.title: Open Mark-Making: No Model, No Pressure
drafts.invitation: If the child draws a line and then sets the crayon down, let them decide whether to return to the paper. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Describe the mark’s path—curved, straight, broken—without naming it or suggesting a shape.
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child returns to the same area to add another mark.

drafts.title: Try an arrangement
drafts.invitation: If the child places a block in a new spot, use the space to explore how it fits with the rest. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Use descriptive language about the placement, like 'This one leans toward the edge.'
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child adjusts a block after placing it.

drafts.title: Try an arrangement
drafts.invitation: If the child shifts a block to a different position, let them see how the shape changes the space. The child can stop or turn away.
drafts.caregiverWords: Let the child lead the movement; describe what shifts without naming the change.
drafts.observation: If you want to, notice whether the child pauses to look at the new layout.
